claims.text: The Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) is an open standard from OpenAI and Stripe for running checkout between an AI agent, a buyer and a business.
The ACP README labels the specification as beta.
The core ACP RFCs, including Agentic Checkout and Delegate Payment, carry the status Draft.
Newer ACP RFCs for capability negotiation, cart, discovery, product feeds, intent traces, affiliate attribution and marketing consent carry the status Proposal.
ACP is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, and the NOTICE file names OpenAI and Stripe as 2025 copyright holders.
The ACP GitHub repository agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol was created on 2025-09-29.
OpenAI announced Instant Checkout in ChatGPT and the open-sourced Agentic Commerce Protocol on 2025-09-29.
Stripe announced on 2025-09-29 that it co-developed ACP with OpenAI and introduced the Shared Payment Token.
MAINTAINERS.md lists OpenAI, Stripe and Meta as lead maintainers of ACP; the file is unchanged at commit 7fdd78d, the last commit through 2026-11-21.
The ACP governance model was revised by PR 173 on 2026-03-10.
The ACP Technical Steering Committee has up to 7 seats, one per organization.
OpenAI and Stripe, as Founding Maintainers, appoint and remove ACP Technical Steering Committee members.
The ACP Technical Steering Committee had three members on 2026-11-21: OpenAI, Stripe and Meta.
Meta was added to the ACP Technical Steering Committee as seat 3 on 2026-04-24.
Significant ACP changes go through Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) with a TSC sponsor, a 7-business-day public review and a simple majority TSC vote.
Standard ACP pull requests need two approvals from TSC members, and one may come from a recognized Domain Working Group member.
OpenAI and Stripe keep a reserve veto over ACP SEPs that can only block a change, never force one, and must come with a written explanation.
ACP has no foundation; its governance document states a long-term goal of moving to a neutral foundation once four conditions are met.
There is no fee to join the ACP Technical Steering Committee or a Domain Working Group.
The ACP TSC holds a weekly 30-minute meeting on Thursday and rotates a weekly triage lead with a 2-business-day initial response target.
ACP contributions require a Contributor License Agreement under a Collaboration and Governance Agreement dated 2025-11-21.
ACP corporate CLA signatories are Stripe, OpenAI, Adyen, Wix, commercetools, OpenCommerce Network, Affirm, Meta, Agentic Commerce Inc. (Catalog) and PayPal.
The ACP CLA list names OpenCommerce Network Inc., not nekuda, as a corporate signatory; a nekuda GitHub user appears among its authorized users.
PayPal signed the ACP corporate CLA on 2026-04-16 and Meta on 2026-03-19.
ACP versions are dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, and clients send the version in the required API-Version header.
The latest released ACP version is 2026-04-17, promoted by PR 227 on 2026-04-17.
The ACP repository has no GitHub releases and no Git tags; versions exist only as dated folders and changelog files.
Version 2025-12-12 renamed fulfillment_address to fulfillment_details and replaced fulfillment_option_id with selected_fulfillment_options.
The 2025-12-12 changelog says its breaking changes came from learnings from URBN and Etsy adapter implementations.
Version 2026-01-16 let merchants name their 3DS authentication provider and added adyen to the provider enums.
Version 2026-01-30 added capability negotiation, the payment handlers framework, the extensions framework and the discount extension.
The payment handlers framework in 2026-01-30 was a breaking change that replaced payment_provider.supported_payment_methods with capabilities.payment.handlers.
Version 2026-04-17 added Cart, the Feed API, Delegate Authentication, the /.well-known/acp.json discovery document and the MCP binding.
Version 2026-04-17 made the Idempotency-Key header mandatory on all POST requests.
Version 2026-04-17 added native orders with line items, fulfillments, adjustments and totals.
The last commit on the ACP main branch is 7fdd78d, SEP: Optional product URL on checkout Item (#281), committed 2026-07-18T04:51:51Z.
Eighteen commits landed on ACP main between 2026-04-24 and 2026-07-18, after the 2026-04-17 release.
No commit landed in the ACP repository between 2026-07-18 and 2026-11-21, and the repository has no tag, release or security advisory; every branch head dates from 2026-07-18 or earlier.
Unreleased ACP changes include suggested pricing on checkout create, fulfillment_details on complete, a feed_update_id on product upserts and an optional product url on checkout items.
Released ACP snapshot folders are edited after release: the 2026-01-30 checkout schema changed six times in February 2026 and the 2026-04-17 folder changed on 2026-05-01 and 2026-06-15.
The ACP repository package.json names the package @agentic-commerce-protocol/specification at version 0.1.0.
The package @agentic-commerce-protocol/specification is not published on npm; the registry returned 404 on 2026-10-11.
In ACP the merchant remains the system of record for orders, payments, taxes and compliance.

OpenAI is not the merchant of record. Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, its ACP docs (read 2026-10-11) said the merchant selling the goods is the merchant of record and that customers see the merchant's name on their card statement; its Accept payments guide says the business handles the order, fulfillment, customer support and fraud decisions (as of 2026-11-14).
Under ACP the merchant handles refunds and chargebacks because it accepted the payment as merchant of record, as OpenAI's ACP docs said until their 2026-11-13 rewrite (read 2026-10-11).
In ACP the agent calls the merchant's checkout endpoints and hosts the order webhook receiver at /agentic_checkout/webhooks/order_events.

OpenAI's plugin Checkout API reference lets a merchant with a PCI DSS Level 1 certificate receive raw card data by implementing the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint (as of 2026-11-14). Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's commerce docs reserved direct integration with its Delegated Payment Spec for PSPs and PCI DSS Level 1 merchants with their own vaults.

The ACP website calls Stripe the first compatible PSP, with its Shared Payment Token (as of 2026-11-14); until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's commerce docs called the SPT the first Delegated Payment Spec-compatible implementation.
The Shared Payment Token is a Stripe product used with ACP, not part of the ACP specification.
The ACP discovery RFC allows a seller platform, for example acp.stripe.com, to host the discovery document on behalf of many sellers.
A 2026-04-17 checkout session requires id, capabilities, status, currency, line_items, fulfillment_options, totals, messages and links.
A 2026-04-17 create checkout request requires line_items, currency and capabilities.
From 2026-01-30 the ACP Item object has only id, name and unit_amount, with id required and no quantity field.
In ACP versions 2025-09-29 through 2026-01-16 the create request used items, and each Item required id and quantity.
The complete checkout request requires payment_data and may carry buyer, authentication_result, affiliate_attribution, risk_signals, marketing_consents and order_notes.
ACP payment_data carries handler_id, an instrument with a type and a credential holding a credential type and token, and an optional billing_address.
The ACP schema gives spt and wallet_token as example credential types; spt is not a fixed enum value.
ACP payment_data also has B2B fields: purchase_order_number, payment_terms (immediate, net_15, net_30, net_60, net_90), due_date and approval_required.
Every ACP PaymentHandler requires id, name, version, spec, requires_delegate_payment, requires_pci_compliance, psp, config_schema, instrument_schemas and config.
ACP payment handler names use reverse-DNS form, for example dev.acp.tokenized.card.
The seller-backed handler family is dev.acp.seller_backed.saved_card, dev.acp.seller_backed.gift_card, dev.acp.seller_backed.points and dev.acp.seller_backed.store_credit.
Seller-backed ACP handlers use requires_delegate_payment true and requires_pci_compliance false, so no card credential moves to the agent.
Version 2026-04-17 added optional display_order and display_name fields to payment handlers; display_order is only a suggestion.
ACP amounts are integers in minor currency units.
ACP Total types in 2026-04-17 are items_base_amount, items_discount, subtotal, discount, fulfillment, tax, fee, gift_wrap, tip, store_credit, total and amount_refunded.
ACP fulfillment option types are shipping, digital, pickup and local_delivery; pickup and local_delivery appear from 2026-01-30.

ACP MessageError codes in 2026-04-17 are missing, invalid, out_of_stock, payment_declined, requires_sign_in, requires_3ds, low_stock, quantity_exceeded, coupon_invalid, coupon_expired, minimum_not_met, maximum_exceeded, region_restricted, age_verification_required, approval_required, unsupported, not_found, conflict, rate_limited, expired and intervention_required.
ACP messages may carry a resolution value of recoverable, requires_buyer_input or requires_buyer_review, added in 2026-04-17.
ACP HTTP-level errors are flat objects with type, code, message and optional param, where type is invalid_request, processing_error or service_unavailable.
Since 2026-04-17 ACP servers SHOULD return a supported_versions array when they reject a missing or unsupported API-Version.
An ACP Order requires id, checkout_session_id and permalink_url.
ACP Order adjustments have defined types refund, credit, return, exchange, price_adjustment, cancellation and dispute, with dispute covering chargebacks.
ACP markdown content must follow CommonMark 0.31.2 and must not contain raw HTML, and agents must render it with raw HTML disabled or sanitized.
The Delegate Payment request requires payment_method, allowance, risk_signals and metadata, with an optional billing_address.
The ACP Allowance requires reason, max_amount, currency, checkout_session_id, merchant_id and expires_at.
The only Allowance reason defined by ACP is one_time.
Delegate Payment accepts only card credentials, with card_number_type set to fpan or network_token.
The Delegate Payment response returns a vault token id that starts with vt_, a created timestamp and metadata, with HTTP 201.
Delegate Payment risk signals have type card_testing, a score and an action of blocked, manual_review or authorized; since 2026-04-17 the array may be empty.
Version 2026-04-17 raised the maximum length of the card iin field from 6 to 8 characters.
The ACP discovery document requires protocol, api_base_url, transports and capabilities, and protocol.name is always acp.
Discovery capabilities.services can list checkout, orders, delegate_payment and carts, and transports can list rest and mcp.
An ACP Cart requires id, line_items, currency and totals, and its totals are estimates.
An ACP feed Product requires id and variants, and each Variant requires id and title.
The ACP IntentTrace reason codes are price_sensitivity, shipping_cost, shipping_speed, product_fit, trust_security, returns_policy, payment_options, comparison, timing_deferred and other.
ACP affiliate attribution requires a provider and supports first-touch at session creation and last-touch at completion.
ACP marketing consent uses marketing_consent_options on the session and marketing_consents with channel and opted_in on the complete request.
The only extension declared through the ACP extensions framework is discount, identified by name discount.
ACP discount responses can include applied discounts with allocations and rejected codes with reasons such as discount_code_expired.
ACP checkout requests require Authorization: Bearer, API-Version and, on POST, Idempotency-Key; Signature, Timestamp and Request-Id are recommended.
POST /checkout_sessions creates an ACP checkout session and returns 201 Created.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id} updates an ACP session and returns the full authoritative state with 200.
GET /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id} returns the session with 200 or 404 if it does not exist.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id}/complete must create an order and return status completed with an order id, checkout_session_id and permalink_url.
The ACP OpenAPI lists 200 as the success code for completing a checkout session.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id}/cancel returns 200 with status canceled, or 405 if the session is already completed or canceled.
A cancel request may carry an intent_trace with a required reason_code, and servers without intent trace support must still accept that body.
Delegate Payment is a single POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment endpoint that issues a token usable by the merchant's PSP only within the Allowance.

OpenAI's plugin Checkout API reference shows the delegated payment request it sends to a PCI DSS Level 1 merchant, with an allowance of reason one_time, max_amount, currency, checkout_session_id, merchant_id and expires_at (as of 2026-11-14). Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, its commerce docs said OpenAI sets the maximum amount and expiry from what the user chose to buy.
When a seller requires 3DS it sets the session status to authentication_required and must include authentication_metadata.
If an agent completes a session in authentication_required without authentication_result, the server must return a 4XX error with code requires_3ds and param $.authentication_result.

ACP Delegate Authentication uses POST /delegate_authentication, POST /delegate_authentication/{authentication_session_id}/authenticate and GET /delegate_authentication/{authentication_session_id} for 3DS2.
In ACP Delegate Authentication the client reports fingerprint_completion as Y, N or U, using N after a 10-second timeout.
ACP sellers declare required interventions with capabilities.interventions.required and enforcement always, conditional or optional.
If an agent cannot handle a required intervention and enforcement is always, the seller should return a message with code intervention_required.
Capability negotiation in ACP uses intersection semantics: the agent declares what it supports and the seller returns the mutual set.
ACP idempotency errors are 400 idempotency_key_required, 422 idempotency_conflict and 409 idempotency_in_flight.
ACP servers must keep idempotency key mappings for at least 24 hours and must not cache 5xx responses against a key.
A replayed ACP response should carry the header Idempotent-Replayed: true.
The ACP cart endpoints are POST /carts, GET /carts/{id}, PUT /carts/{id} and POST /carts/{id}/cancel.
ACP carts are scoped to a single seller and have no status, no payment data and no capability negotiation.
The ACP Feed API is hosted by the agent and called by merchants, a push model with POST /feeds, GET /feeds/{id}, GET /feeds/{id}/products and PATCH /feeds/{id}/products.
ACP feed file ingestion uses metadata.json and products.jsonl and replaces the whole product set; promotions were deferred.

Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's commerce docs described an OpenAI feed API on /product_feeds paths with a promotions API (read 2026-10-11). The rewritten docs document no feed API; OpenAI's Ads API instead updates existing feed variants with PATCH /feeds/{feed_id}/products (as of 2026-11-14).

As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's commerce docs recommended a full feed once a day by file upload plus API updates during the day. Since the 2026-11-13 rewrite they describe only full snapshots by manual upload, a hosted URL or SFTP, while OpenAI's Ads docs pair SFTP catalog uploads with a Delta Feeds API for title, price and availability changes (as of 2026-11-14).

Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's commerce docs limited feed onboarding to approved partners who apply through a form. The rewritten docs send businesses to Business Hub, where a business claims its profile and must verify its identity before uploading products, while OpenAI's merchant page still shows an application form and a waitlist (as of 2026-11-14).
The ACP discovery document lives at /.well-known/acp.json, needs no authentication and should be cached with at least Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600.
Payment handlers are not in the ACP discovery document; they are returned per session on POST /checkout_sessions.
ACP 2025-09-29 defined five checkout statuses: not_ready_for_payment, ready_for_payment, completed, canceled and in_progress.
The checkout status authentication_required first appears in the ACP 2025-12-12 schema, not in 2026-01-30.
ACP 2026-01-30 added the checkout statuses incomplete, requires_escalation, pending_approval, complete_in_progress and expired, for 11 statuses in total.
The checkout RFC's status list still names only the original five statuses; the six later values appear only in the JSON Schema, and only authentication_required gets behavior in the RFC text.
Stripe Shared Payment Tokens have the statuses active, requires_action and deactivated, and deactivated is terminal.

A Stripe SPT is deactivated when it is consumed, expires or is revoked; by 2026-10-20 (absent from the 2026-09-21 capture of the seller page) the same page adds resolved, when the seller exchanges it through the Resolve API.
ACP Delegate Authentication create returns action_required, pending or not_supported.
The 2026-04-17 ACP Order status values are created, confirmed, manual_review, processing, shipped, completed and canceled, after an edit on 2026-05-01.
ACP's MCP binding maps the five checkout operations to the tools create_checkout_session, get_checkout_session, update_checkout_session, complete_checkout_session and cancel_checkout_session.
The ACP MCP binding uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over MCP Streamable HTTP with arguments meta, id and payload.
In the ACP MCP binding, authorization moves to MCP server configuration and ACP errors use JSON-RPC code -32000.
The ACP MCP binding was added on 2026-02-19 by PR 139 and released in version 2026-04-17.
The ACP checkout RFC says TLS 1.3 must be used, while OpenAI's production guide, as read on 2026-10-11 and removed in the 2026-11-13 rewrite, asked for TLS 1.2 or later on port 443.
ACP request signatures are detached signatures over canonical JSON, base64url-encoded in the Signature header, with algorithms agreed out of band.
The Delegate Payment RFC gives Ed25519 and ES256 as example signature algorithms.
ACP order webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, a dot and the raw body, sent as Merchant-Signature: t=<unix_seconds>,v1=<64_hex>.
The recommended timestamp tolerance for ACP webhook signatures is 300 seconds, and receivers reject failures with 401.
The ACP changelog says the Merchant-Signature format aligns with Stripe's webhook signature scheme.
ACP does not use verifiable credentials, user-signed mandates, RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures or on-chain components.

As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's ACP docs said it intended to move entirely to network tokens as they become supported and that eligible cards are upgraded through network tokenization; the 2026-11-13 rewrite removed that page.

The merchant authenticates an ACP agent with a bearer token agreed out of band, and the agent verifies merchant webhooks with a shared HMAC secret. The spec has no agent registry or public key directory.

OpenAI publishes egress IP ranges for ChatGPT integrations (plugins, connectors, GPT Actions and agentic commerce) and says an IP allowlist does not replace request authentication. For its cloud browser, OpenAI's agent access guide (undated, read 2026-11-21) recommends adding ChatGPT's agent profile to the firewall's allowlist and verifying the request signatures before applying that exception. Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's ACP docs asked merchants to allowlist those egress ranges for ACP calls.
The Delegate Payment RFC says in one section that the client must sign requests, while its header list marks Signature as recommended and the OpenAPI marks it optional.
No GitHub security advisory exists for the ACP repository as of 2026-11-14 (the repository and global advisory APIs return none), and an NVD keyword search returned no CVE on 2026-10-20.
A 2026 Tamarin analysis models ACP together with x402, MPP and AP2 and reports 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency findings across the four protocols.
A 2026 paper says protocols such as AP2 and ACP lack interoperable, tamper-evident audit trails.
ACP has native spending caps through allowance.max_amount and currency.
ACP scopes a delegated token to one merchant and one checkout session through allowance.merchant_id and allowance.checkout_session_id.
ACP has no revocation endpoint; revocation exists in Stripe's SPT product.
ACP supports step-up authentication through the authentication_required status and 3DS2 Delegate Authentication.
ACP has no reputation mechanism.

As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's ACP docs said the Product Feed Spec and Agentic Checkout Spec carry no cardholder data, while direct Delegate Payment integration handles cardholder data and is likely in PCI scope; the 2026-11-13 rewrite removed those pages.

As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's ACP docs said OpenAI may require a PCI attestation of compliance before enabling production Delegate Payment access; the commerce docs rewritten on 2026-11-13 do not mention PCI (search 2026-11-14).
ACP implementations must not log full card numbers or CVC values.

OpenAI's Commerce policies (updated 2026-09-29) set eligibility standards for product listings and merchant participation in its shopping experiences. They bar alcoholic beverages over 0.5% ABV and distillation kits, tobacco and nicotine products, firearms and other weapons, illegal or regulated drugs, prescription-only medications, supplements, gambling and adult sexual content, and OpenAI's Business Hub help article says products in a feed must follow them. OpenAI's plugin guidelines keep a separate prohibited-goods list for plugins that does not name alcohol (as of 2026-11-21). OpenAI's ACP docs, as read on 2026-10-11, also listed alcohol among products excluded from ChatGPT shopping.
Stripe Shared Payment Tokens are available to agents, customers and sellers in the US, Canada and listed European countries.
ACP order webhooks use the event types order_create and order_update.

As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's production checklist named the webhooks order_created and order_updated, which differs from the spec's order_create and order_update; the checklist was removed in the 2026-11-13 rewrite.
Version 2026-04-17 removed refunds[] from webhook order data in favor of adjustments[].
Stripe sends shared_payment.issued_token.requires_action, .active, .used and .deactivated events to agents, and shared_payment.granted_token.deactivated to sellers.
There is no public explorer, indexer or registry of ACP merchants; the ACP site says discovery mechanisms were still being developed.

Stripe SPTs carry usage_limits with currency, max_amount and expires_at, and the agent sets max_amount to the transaction total. For recurring charges a seller reuses the SPT in each PaymentIntent, which works only when usage_limits.recurring_interval is set (as of 2026-11-14).
A seller uses an SPT by confirming a PaymentIntent with payment_method_data[shared_payment_granted_token], and Stripe clones the customer's original PaymentMethod.
Stripe lists cards, Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna and Affirm (limited) as SPT payment methods.

Stripe says it might use tokens from Mastercard Agent Pay and Visa Intelligent Commerce on a seller's behalf for SPT card payments. By 2026-10-20 (absent from the 2026-09-21 capture of the seller page) the seller page also names American Express ACE Kit; the agent page names Mastercard and Visa only.
Stripe's launch release says SPTs are scoped to a specific merchant and basket total.
Stripe's Agentic Commerce Suite for agents is a private preview with a waitlist, available in the US, Canada and select European countries, for purchases of physical goods.
At launch, US ChatGPT Plus, Pro and Free users could buy from US Etsy sellers through Instant Checkout, with over a million Shopify merchants announced as coming soon.
Instant Checkout supported only single-item purchases at launch.
OpenAI said at launch that Instant Checkout items are not preferred in product results, though Instant Checkout availability is one ranking factor among several.
Walmart announced on 2025-10-14 that customers would soon be able to shop Walmart in ChatGPT using Instant Checkout.
PayPal announced on 2025-10-28 that it will adopt ACP, support Instant Checkout through the delegated payments API and run an ACP server for its merchants.
Stripe launched the Agentic Commerce Suite on 2025-12-11, naming platforms including Squarespace, Wix, Etsy, WooCommerce, commercetools and BigCommerce.
Microsoft launched Copilot Checkout on 2026-01-08 in the US with PayPal, Shopify and Stripe and said it is adopting open standards like ACP.
Microsoft's later agentic commerce page says Microsoft Merchant Center will support UCP and requires a UCP-compliant feed for Copilot Checkout.
Trade press reported in March 2026 an OpenAI spokesperson statement that Instant Checkout is moving to apps.
Shopify's president said on 2026-03-03 that only around a dozen merchants on the platform were selling through AI tools including ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI said the initial Instant Checkout lacked the flexibility it wanted and let merchants use their own checkout while it focused on product discovery.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI expanded ACP to product discovery, with merchants sharing product feeds and promotions through ACP.
OpenAI named Target, Sephora, Nordstrom, Lowe's, Best Buy, The Home Depot and Wayfair as retailers integrated into ACP for discovery on 2026-03-24.

OpenAI said Shopify product data reaches ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog with no extra merchant work, and quoted Shopify's VP of Product saying buyers complete purchases on the merchant's online store through an in-app browser.
OpenAI named Salesforce and Stripe as third-party providers that can deliver merchant feeds through ACP.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI described a Walmart app in ChatGPT with account linking, loyalty and Walmart payments.
External checkout, where users finish on the merchant's own site, is the recommended and generally available checkout path for ChatGPT plugins (formerly the Apps SDK).
Checkout with the ChatGPT payment sheet is a private beta limited to select marketplace partners.
With the ChatGPT payment sheet, the plugin widget calls requestCheckout and ChatGPT sends a payment-method token to the merchant's MCP server in a complete_checkout tool call.
OpenAI lists Adyen, Checkout.com, Fiserv, PayPal, Stripe and Worldpay as PSPs that support processing for the ChatGPT payment sheet.
Merchants with a PCI DSS Level 1 certificate can receive raw card data for the ChatGPT payment sheet by implementing the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint, including allowance constraints.
No source read says the general ChatGPT payment sheet token is an allowance-scoped delegated token.

Stripe's agentic commerce docs keep a protocol page each for ACP and UCP. Its seller guides name UCP for merchants who run their own checkout, and its Agentic Commerce Suite page says it accepts payments across multiple commerce protocols.
There is no official ACP SDK from OpenAI or Stripe; npm and PyPI packages named agentic-commerce-protocol are third-party type definitions published by Svix.
The ACP repository validates its JSON Schemas and examples in CI with scripts/validate-consistency.js and ajv.
OpenAI said on 2025-09-29 that merchants pay a small fee on completed Instant Checkout purchases and that the service is free for users.
OpenAI's merchant page says shoppers go to the merchant's site or app by default with no fees for purchases made there (as of 2026-11-14; the same sentence is in a 2026-04-04 capture).
PYMNTS reported, citing The Information and a Shopify spokesperson, that Shopify merchants would pay OpenAI 4% on ChatGPT checkout sales on top of Shopify fees.
The same report said checkouts in Google's AI Mode and Gemini and in Microsoft Copilot carried no additional fee for now.
ACP itself charges no protocol fee; merchants pay their own PSP's processing fees because they charge the payment.

Stripe's US pricing page lists Shared Payment Tokens at 0.15 USD per SPT issued and does not say which party is billed; archived copies show the price from 2026-04-23 on, while Stripe's agentic commerce and SPT docs pages show no price.
OpenAI said more than 700 million people use ChatGPT each week when it launched Instant Checkout.
No official ACP transaction volume, GMV or merchant count has been published by OpenAI, Stripe or the ACP project.

The ACP GitHub repository had 1,607 stars, 260 forks and 151 open issues and pull requests (93 issues, 58 pull requests) on 2026-11-21, against 1,602 stars and 260 forks on 2026-11-14 and 1,583 stars and 256 forks on 2026-10-20.
ACP has no documented relation to ERC-8004.
ERC-8183, a Draft created 2026-02-25, calls itself the Agentic Commerce Protocol but is an on-chain job escrow standard unrelated to OpenAI and Stripe's ACP.

ACP has no documented relation to x402. As of 2026-10-12 Stripe's hub listed x402 with MPP for machine payments and UCP or ACP for agent selling. By 2026-10-20 it names MPP and x402 for machine payments and gives ACP and UCP separate protocol pages.
ACP has no documented relation to Visa TAP; ACP agents authenticate with bearer tokens and optional detached signatures.
ACP and UCP have no bridge or mapping specification.
ACP and UCP share five checkout status names: incomplete, requires_escalation, complete_in_progress, completed and canceled.
UCP uses ready_for_complete where ACP uses ready_for_payment.
ACP publishes discovery at /.well-known/acp.json and UCP at /.well-known/ucp.
Stripe says it is a member of the UCP Tech Council while also co-maintaining ACP.
Stripe's MPP integration accepts cards through Shared Payment Tokens, the token the ACP website names when it calls Stripe the first compatible PSP.
Stripe's guide for monetizing an MCP server, which replaced its ChatGPT apps page, shows an agent paying an MCP tool's payment link with an SPT through MPP.
ACP has no AP2-style mandates, so it carries no signed proof of user intent beyond scoped tokens and the agent's own confirmation UI.
The Verifiable Intent project proposes carrying its credentials in ACP's extension mechanism; this is a proposal, not an adopted ACP extension.
ACP has no documented relation to Mastercard Agent Pay in the spec, but Agent Pay tokens can sit under Stripe SPT card payments.
The ChatGPT payment sheet uses a plugin (formerly Apps SDK) MCP tool named complete_checkout, which is not the ACP MCP binding's complete_checkout_session.
ACP RFC and OpenAPI request examples still send items with id and quantity, which do not validate against the 2026-04-17 schema that requires line_items without quantity.
The ACP checkout RFC still carries the header Version: 2026-01-16 after the 2026-04-17 release.
The ACP MCP binding keeps the idempotency key optional and lists request_not_idempotent, although REST 2026-04-17 made the header required and removed that error type.
As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's ACP docs said idempotency_conflict returns HTTP 409, while the ACP spec uses 422 for that code; the 2026-11-13 rewrite removed those docs.
As read on 2026-10-11, OpenAI's production checklist expected 201 Created on order completion, while the ACP OpenAPI lists 200; the checklist was removed in the 2026-11-13 rewrite.
The 2026-04-17 changelog lists the order status delivered, but the edited 2026-04-17 schema lists completed instead.
The 2026-01-30 ACP changelog deprecates a version 2026-01-22 that has no spec folder.
The ACP checkout OpenAPI describes the Signature header as an HMAC signature for webhook verification, which does not match the RFC's detached request signature.
The flagship ChatGPT Instant Checkout in its 2025 form was scaled back in March 2026.

Until the 2026-11-13 rewrite, OpenAI's commerce docs described supporting Instant Checkout in ChatGPT as three flows: product feed, checkout and payments. The rewritten docs no longer describe Instant Checkout, while OpenAI's plugin guidelines still list it as a beta for select marketplace partners (as of 2026-11-14).
ACP is not IBM's Agent Communication Protocol, which merged into A2A under the Linux Foundation in an announcement dated 2025-08-29.
The PyPI package acp-sdk is IBM's Agent Communication Protocol SDK, not an SDK for the Agentic Commerce Protocol.
ACP is not Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol, which Virtuals describes as the commerce layer of its on-chain agent economy.
ACP is not the Agent Client Protocol, a protocol for connecting editors to agents.
A 2025 survey of MCP, ACP, A2A and ANP uses ACP to mean IBM's Agent Communication Protocol.

The 2026 SoK on agentic commerce security lists an Agent Commerce Protocol next to ERC-8183 and states that ACP in the paper refers exclusively to Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol, not OpenAI and Stripe's ACP.
OpenAI's launch post says users confirm each step and that payment tokens are authorized only for specific amounts and merchants with the user's permission.
ACP lets agents embed commerce without becoming the merchant of record, according to its README.
The Stripe launch release says ChatGPT passes the SPT to the merchant, which can process through Stripe or another provider while using Stripe's risk scores.

Stripe's Shared Payment Token documentation page is labeled Public preview and shows no price; the price, 0.15 USD per SPT issued, is on Stripe's US pricing page, whose Learn more link opens the agent variant of that documentation page.
A secondary report says Shopify Agentic Storefronts carry a per-channel fee set in Shopify Admin on top of payment processing, with the rate not public.
The repository's own 2026-04-17 examples file sends line_items with only an item id, which matches the JSON Schema.
Delegate Payment error codes are invalid_card, duplicate_request, idempotency_conflict, too_many_requests, idempotency_key_required and idempotency_in_flight.
ACP states the allowance limits but defines no token status field and no error code that a PSP returns when a token is used outside its allowance.
On ACP checkout requests the Timestamp check is only a SHOULD, so request freshness is not enforced by the spec.
The 2026-04-17 changelog says Item.quantity became a number, but only the 2025-09-29 schema has that type; later schemas keep integer or drop the field.
The discovery document lists supported_versions oldest first, and the last entry is the latest version the seller supports.
Converting an ACP cart into a checkout session was deferred in the cart RFC.
ACP's mission document says the protocol aims to be open and neutral, agnostic to agents, PSPs, sellers, transports and payment methods.
ACP fulfillment status values are pending, processing, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, ready_for_pickup, delivered, failed and canceled.
ACP adjustment status values are pending, completed and failed, and implementations must accept unknown values.
Since 2026-04-17 a missing Merchant-Signature, a malformed one, one outside the time window or one that fails verification is rejected with 401.
The Delegate Payment RFC marks PaymentMethodCard.virtual as required while the JSON Schema makes it optional.

OpenAI's merchant page, read 2026-10-20 and again 2026-11-14, says shopping is live for US ChatGPT users and applicants wait on a waitlist. Shopify and Etsy catalogs are already integrated with no setup, and a self-serve merchant platform is planned later in the year; the page does not mention Businesses in ChatGPT (introduced 2026-11-10) or Business Hub.
OpenAI's plugin checkout reference says approval for external checkout is currently limited to plugins for physical goods purchases.
A ChatGPT plugin can offer checkout with payment methods already saved with the merchant without leaving ChatGPT; this path cannot collect new credentials, which need the ChatGPT payment sheet.
Stripe's ACP protocol page describes ACP as created by Stripe, OpenAI and Meta; the repository NOTICE names OpenAI and Stripe, and Meta's TSC seat dates from 2026-04-24.

Stripe's SPT Resolve API lets a seller resolve a granted token once into one of three credential types, fpan, agentic_token or dpan, for a third-party processor (as of 2026-11-14; the 2026-10-20 read also listed network_token). Unless the seller has given Stripe a PCI Attestation of Compliance, Stripe encrypts in-scope credentials with a key the seller cannot read.

Between 2026-07-18 and 2026-11-14 no ACP maintainer commented, reviewed, merged or committed; the 67 issue and pull request comments in that window, 19 of them after 2026-10-20, came from non-members. The one maintainer action was closing SEP PR 178 unmerged on 2026-08-09.

PR 316 (opened 2026-10-16), a dispute-resolution extension SEP, is marked proposal awaiting a sponsor; a comment on 2026-11-06 marked it ready for maintainer review, and no maintainer had replied by 2026-11-21, after a new commit on 2026-11-16 and a 2026-11-18 comment asking Meta's TSC representative to sponsor it. Issue 315 (2026-10-15) says the merchant has no stored agent identity.
The README says OpenAI and Stripe first implemented ACP and calls their hosted services production-ready reference implementations.
The repository's 2026-04-17 example of a declined payment is a checkout session object whose messages carry the code payment_declined, not an HTTP error response.
URBN is the retail group behind Urban Outfitters, Anthropologie and Free People.

The FAQ on OpenAI's merchant page says "There are no fees on purchases that start in ChatGPT" and that OpenAI is moving away from a standalone Instant Checkout experience, with purchases completed on merchant-owned websites or apps (as of 2026-11-14; already in a 2026-04-04 capture).

On 2026-11-13 OpenAI announced ChatGPT Wallet, rolling out first in dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards. As read 2026-11-21, the post says Wallet was built in partnership with American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa; its launch-day text, as captured at 2026-11-13T16:04:07Z, and launch-day coverage named American Express, Mastercard and Visa, and OpenAI did not mark the change.

OpenAI's Wallet post says the user adds a card once, reviews the items, total and card before each purchase and approves with a security check such as Face ID, and that the payment network then provides a payment token with a card number, security code and expiry, so neither the business nor the agent sees the actual card details.

OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet post never mentions the Agentic Commerce Protocol, Instant Checkout, Delegate Payment or Shared Payment Tokens, and OpenAI's rewritten commerce docs do not mention ACP either (search 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's Wallet help article (updated 2026-11-19) says Wallet works in conversations with a dot and is not available in Chat, Work or standalone Codex threads, while the post's own page description and OpenAI's RSS summary still name agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots (as read 2026-11-21).

OpenAI says it works on ChatGPT Wallet with fraud prevention partners including Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd and with payment service providers including Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe; neither list is presented as complete.

OpenAI's Accept payments guide says ChatGPT Wallet works with a merchant's existing checkout pages and payment forms with no Wallet-specific integration; the merchant receives a network token instead of the card number and can use the Payment Account Reference (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's Accept payments guide says a Wallet customer consents only to the specific transaction, so the merchant must not reuse or save the credential for another purchase; subscriptions need the customer's consent and follow the processor's practice for merchant-initiated transactions (as of 2026-11-14).

For Wallet purchases OpenAI says the business handles the order, fulfillment, customer support and fraud decisions, and its agent access FAQ says customers bear final responsibility for the actions they take; that is OpenAI's position, not a liability rule (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI is rolling out user signals in the Forwarded HTTP header for its cloud browser, with the parameters asn, for, ip-country, ip-prefix, locale, tz and user-agent. IANA's registry lists only by, for, host and proto, so six of the seven are unregistered extensions, and RFC 7239 warns that any node on the path can alter the header (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's agent access guide says ChatGPT uses Web Bot Auth to identify certain cloud browser requests: Signature and Signature-Input headers plus a Signature-Agent of https://chatgpt.com, with keys in chatgpt.com's well-known HTTP message signatures directory, verified automatically by Akamai, Cloudflare, HUMAN and Vercel. This is ChatGPT's own mechanism; the ACP specification does not use Web Bot Auth (as of 2026-11-21).
OpenAI's agent access FAQ says it requires human review before any consequential action across all users, and that site owners cannot yet control which actions users take (as of 2026-11-14).

Between 2026-11-12T03:49Z and 2026-11-13T17:12Z OpenAI replaced its ACP developer docs at developers.openai.com/commerce with the Commerce in ChatGPT Partner Playbook, which covers agent access, accepting payments, building a plugin, claiming a business, Sign in with ChatGPT, product feeds and a feed schema; the old ACP pages redirect to it or answer 404.

OpenAI's merchant page says ChatGPT shopping is built on ACP, calls ACP the open infrastructure for AI-native commerce in ChatGPT, and says it supports product discovery today and will expand to the full shopping journey (as of 2026-11-21; the same text is in a 2026-04-04 capture).

OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT on 2026-11-10. Its product feeds guide sends businesses to Business Hub, where a business claims its profile, verifies its identity before uploading products and delivers full catalog snapshots by manual upload, a hosted URL or SFTP; the feed does not update a cart or confirm a purchase (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's Ads API has a Delta Feeds API, PATCH /feeds/{feed_id}/products, that updates the title, price or availability of existing variants and answers 200 with the feed id and accepted true; it is enabled per ad account. Its path pattern and its id and accepted response match ACP 2026-04-17's feed upsert (PATCH /feeds/{id}/products), and OpenAI does not name ACP (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's product feed schema has a Stable view in OpenAI's own flat format, with prices in major units such as 79.99 USD, and a Draft view, published for planning and feedback only, that follows ACP 2026-04-17's Product and Variant feed model with integer minor units; neither view names ACP (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's product checkout conversion spec for plugins now says its nested checkout session uses the data shape of a legacy checkout specification, which it links to ACP's 2025-09-29 checkout OpenAPI; until at least 2026-11-06 it pointed to OpenAI's own commerce checkout docs (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's commerce plugin guide recommends a headless MCP plugin, says iframe-based MCP UI is not supported in dots, and has a plugin return a continue_url browser handoff when it cannot finish checkout; OpenAI says it is still working out how third-party plugins interact with ChatGPT Wallet (as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's 2026-11-13 commerce plugin guide shows a reference checkout whose field names and enums match UCP's checkout schema (an item with id, title and price; totals with only type and amount; message severity requires_buyer_input with a path), not ACP 2026-04-17's (an item with id, name and unit_amount; totals with display_text; severity from info to critical with a separate resolution). The guide credits an unnamed cart and checkout proposal and names neither protocol; its cart and product lookup shapes are OpenAI's own.

Meta, which holds ACP TSC seat 3, launched its shopping agent Muse on 2026-09-08 paying through Link by Stripe, and its Connect post of 2026-09-24 lists Shop Pay and PayPal for payments; Stripe says Link gives Muse single-use virtual cards where Link is not accepted. No Meta or Stripe post on Muse mentions ACP (as of 2026-11-14).

Sierra announced the Personal Agent Protocol on 2026-10-06 as an open standard it develops with Meta, with partners including Shopify, Stripe and Walmart, and listed OpenAI and PayPal among its design partners on 2026-10-09. Its PAP 1.0 post (2026-11-13) leaves product search, carts and checkout to UCP, linked through a commerce extension that Shopify co-authored, and none of the three posts mentions ACP; a design partner is not an implementer.

Mastercard's CEO said on the 2026-10-29 earnings call that Mastercard had signed a broad strategic partnership with OpenAI that includes the use of Agent Pay (a third-party transcript; Mastercard's written results do not mention it). No source names the network program behind ChatGPT Wallet tokens (as of 2026-11-14).

Visa announced a strategic collaboration with OpenAI on 2026-06-10 as part of Visa Intelligent Commerce. No source ties ChatGPT Wallet to Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol or to Visa Intelligent Commerce tokens, and ChatGPT's cloud browser identifies itself with plain Web Bot Auth (as of 2026-11-14).
OpenAI's Wallet post quotes American Express calling ChatGPT Wallet its first Agentic Commerce Experiences integration (2026-11-13).

Stripe's Link Agent Wallet returns a payment credential for each spend request the customer approves: a virtual card (one-time or recurring), a Shared Payment Token for APIs that accept SPTs directly or for MPP with method stripe, or a Link Pay Token for Stripe-enabled checkouts. Stripe says Link powers payments for more than 200 personal agents (company figure, 2026-10-21); its Link pages do not mention ACP (as of 2026-11-14).

PSPs still document ACP for ChatGPT as of 2026-11-14: Checkout.com announced ACP support on 2025-11-25 and documents a delegated payment token for ChatGPT plugins, Worldpay documents POST /sessions/agentic_commerce/delegate_payment as an approved Instant Checkout partner, and PayPal's Agent Ready lists ACP for ChatGPT through Braintree delegated tokens.

Shopify's Help Center calls its ChatGPT channel a discovery-focused referrer: purchases complete in the store's own checkout, with no fees for selling in ChatGPT beyond standard payment processing. Shopify's Fall '26 developer post (2026-10-28) offers the same catalog and checkout to any agent through Shop.dev and names neither ACP nor UCP (as of 2026-11-14).
OpenAI's Wallet post gives 1.2B weekly ChatGPT users (OpenAI's figure, 2026-11-13).

The ACP README still lists OpenAI's documentation as a production-ready reference implementation, but the link now opens the Commerce in ChatGPT Partner Playbook, which documents no ACP implementation (as of 2026-11-21).
CNBC reports that OpenAI is not taking a cut of ChatGPT Wallet transactions to start; OpenAI's Wallet post states no fee (as of 2026-11-14).

ACP-era wording survives on other OpenAI pages as of 2026-11-14: the site-wide developer index still lists the commerce docs as the Agentic Commerce Protocol, the plugin Checkout API reference keeps the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint for PCI DSS Level 1 merchants, and the plugin guidelines still name Instant Checkout.

ACP's MCP binding links the Streamable HTTP transport of MCP revision 2025-11-25. MCP's current revision is 2026-07-28, which removed the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id sessions, and the binding has not been revised since (no ACP commit after 2026-07-18, as of 2026-11-14).

OpenAI's Wallet help article (updated 2026-11-19) lists eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards and requires the user to be 18 or older, live in the US and have a US billing address for the card. Chase takes part as the issuer of eligible Chase credit cards: only the primary cardholder can add one, and the user approves the connection in the Chase mobile app, by QR code when starting on a computer. Some US-issued debit cards are supported, but Chase debit cards are not, and virtual cards cannot be added at launch (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's Wallet help article says approving a purchase requires biometric verification, such as Face ID or Touch ID, on a supported device, and its dots controls page says each Wallet payment is reviewed and approved with biometrics. Its Enterprise guide says Wallet is off by default for Enterprise workspaces and that admins will be able to grant a Use Wallet capability once the setting is available, without giving a date (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet terms (effective 2026-11-12) say that after the user approves a purchase, OpenAI may ask a payment service provider, card network or issuer to create or provide a tokenized, virtual or other payment credential linked to the card, which may differ from the printed card number. The terms let the user approve each purchase before it is submitted or grant ChatGPT the authority to approve each purchase in advance, and they say Wallet creates no bank account or stored balance, extends no credit and transfers no funds.

The ChatGPT Wallet terms make the merchant the seller and merchant of record and say OpenAI is not a bank, card issuer, payment network, lender or merchant for Wallet purchases and does not hold purchase funds. OpenAI does not decide or fund merchant refunds or card chargebacks unless required by law or separately promised, the cardholder agreement and issuer and network rules, including dispute rights, still apply, and OpenAI may set transaction, merchant, category, card, account, device or geographic limits (effective 2026-11-12).

OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet Privacy Notice (effective 2026-11-12, issued by OpenAI OpCo, LLC) says a service provider collects the card number, expiration date and security code, while OpenAI receives a tokenized payment credential and limited card details such as the network, issuer, last four digits and billing country or postal code. OpenAI says it does not sell Wallet information or share it for cross-context behavioral or targeted advertising.

OpenAI's Wallet help article says that after approval the dot uses a virtual card number linked to the selected card, so the number entered at checkout may differ from the physical card, and that a ready-to-check-out status means the approval is complete, not that the merchant placed the order; Wallet may not complete checkout at every store. If the user agrees to a recurring plan, the merchant may store the credential and charge it again. The merchant handles returns and refunds, the card issuer handles disputed or unrecognized charges, and OpenAI Support handles Wallet errors and purchases that differ from the approval (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI's agent access guide (undated, read 2026-11-21) recommends that sites add ChatGPT's agent profile to their firewall's allowlist, while keeping other security controls in place, so that cloud browser visits on a user's behalf go through reliably, and that they verify the signatures before applying an allowlist exception for signed requests. It is a recommendation: OpenAI's companion page says to change settings only if security settings block verified visits, and a Vercel-hosted site whose rules do not block the traffic needs no extra configuration.

OpenAI's agent access guide names ChatGPT's cloud browser traffic by provider: ChatGPT Agent in Akamai's AI Fetchers and Agents category and in HUMAN's lists, dots, OpenAI under Cloudflare's Personal Agents or bot tag chatgpt-agent with detection ID 129220581 for Cloudflare WAF rules, and chatgpt-operator at Vercel; all four verify the signatures automatically (read 2026-11-21).

From 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-21 the ACP repository received 26 issue and pull request comments, two of them from the CLA assistant bot and none from an account with a maintainer role, and no pull request review, label or merge; the only closes were two issues closed by their own authors. None of the TSC representatives for OpenAI, Stripe and Meta listed in docs/governance.md commented (read 2026-11-21).

Open community proposals on 2026-11-21, none sponsored, accepted or merged, include SEP issue 325 (2026-11-10), which would bind complete to the session state and the purchase the buyer approved and answer 409 with session_changed or purchase_changed on a mismatch; PR 326 (2026-11-14), which would require meta.idempotency_key for the create, update, complete and cancel MCP tools in the unreleased OpenRPC schema; and SEP issue 329 with PR 330 (2026-11-16 and 2026-11-18), which propose Verifiable Approval Receipts, two optional fields, receipt_id and profile, that point to independently verifiable evidence that the executed order matched what the user approved.

At commit 7fdd78d the Delegate Authentication RFC lists the Signature header as required and says it must be verified, while the Delegate Payment RFC lists it as recommended and says it should be verified, although its request rules say the client must compute a detached signature and place it in the Signature header. The Delegate Authentication RFC is not consistent either: its initialization section says the client should sign, and its OpenAPI file marks the Signature header optional. The discovery RFC defers public signing-key advertisement in JSON Web Key (JWK) format, for verifying the authenticity of responses, until ACP's request signing is formalized.

A community security review filed as issue 331 on 2026-11-20 says ACP's agent-to-merchant request signing is inconsistent and under-specified and weakest on delegate_payment, the endpoint that carries the full card number; it is a community issue, not a GitHub security advisory, and it had no maintainer response on 2026-11-21.

OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT in beta on 2026-11-10. Its release note and help article require Persona identity verification before a business can publish changes, view insights, connect a product feed or create a Business Agent. Business Agents, for eligible US ecommerce and online service businesses, explain products and policies and link to the business's website; they cannot complete purchases, make bookings or check orders, and the Business Agents Policy bars instructing one to submit a form, booking or purchase without explicit authorization through an approved feature (as of 2026-11-21).

OpenAI said on 2025-12-08 that the Instacart app in ChatGPT was the first app to offer a checkout experience directly within ChatGPT, powered by the Agentic Commerce Protocol: users sign in with an Instacart account and check out through OpenAI Instant Checkout without leaving the chat. Instacart's release of the same day says Stripe powers the transactions.

No source found on 2026-11-21 says whether the Instacart app's in-chat checkout still runs; a web search returned nothing newer than the December 2025 launch coverage, and OpenAI's merchant page says OpenAI is moving away from a standalone Instant Checkout experience.
